about: Per-species fine-tunes for the herd aggregation rule (pipeline/herds.py). Each entry is a recorded correction to the general rule, with its reason and source. Read on every build of the herds step; change the data, not the code.

ovis_canadensis.reason: bighorn sheep stay within a few hundred metres of escape terrain (cliffs, steep broken slopes) and do not gather on valley floors; the general rule's flat, low ground is inverted for them
ovis_canadensis.source: Geist, V. (1971). Mountain Sheep: A Study in Behavior and Evolution. University of Chicago Press; Smith, Flinders and Winn (1991), Great Basin Naturalist 51: 205-225 (escape terrain within 300 m)

oreamnos_americanus.reason: mountain goats live on cliffs and the steep slopes beside them
oreamnos_americanus.source: Festa-Bianchet, M. and Cote, S. D. (2008). Mountain Goats: Ecology, Behavior and Conservation of an Alpine Ungulate. Island Press

bison_bison.reason: the rut is mid-July to mid-August; the bulls join the cow groups then and leave them in bachelor bands for the rest of the year

cervus_canadensis.reason: the elk rut is September and October: a herd bull holds a harem in the cow herd
cervus_canadensis.source: Clutton-Brock, Guinness and Albon (1982). Red Deer: Behavior and Ecology of Two Sexes. University of Chicago Press

odocoileus_hemionus.reason: the mule deer rut is November to December
odocoileus_hemionus.source: Wallmo, O. C. (ed.) (1981). Mule and Black-tailed Deer of North America. University of Nebraska Press
